paraphrase: Reciting the four Vedas, bathing in sacred waters and performing rites do not bring one to the Lord who is within; without knowing the One in the body, all such learning is empty.
speaker: Sivavākkiyar
notes: Recalled from memory (no local e-text); cited by incipit because verse numbers differ between editions. No original given. A thematic summary of several verses; low confidence on any single verse's wording.

paraphrase: Milk once drawn does not return to the udder, churned butter does not return to the buttermilk, the sound of the broken conch and the life do not return to the body, fallen flowers and fruit do not go back to the tree: the dead are not born again — no, no, no.
speaker: Sivavākkiyar
notes: Recalled from memory (no local e-text); cited by incipit because verse numbers differ between editions. No original given. Wording of the images recalled with moderate confidence; the verse's scope (all the dead, or the realized) is disputed — see dsp:siddhar-rebirth.

paraphrase: What is a temple, what are sacred tanks? You who worship temples and tanks: the temple is within the mind, the tanks are within the mind; there is no coming to be and no perishing.
speaker: Sivavākkiyar
notes: Recalled from memory (no local e-text); cited by incipit because verse numbers differ between editions. No original given.

paraphrase: You plant a stone and call it god, strew four flowers on it, circle it and mutter mantras — will the planted stone speak, when the Lord is within? Does the cooking pot or the ladle know the taste of the curry?
speaker: Sivavākkiyar
notes: Recalled from memory (no local e-text); cited by incipit because verse numbers differ between editions. No original given.

paraphrase: Running and running, searching and searching for the light that is mingled within, the days pass; withering and withering, crores upon crores of men have died.
speaker: Sivavākkiyar
notes: Recalled from memory (no local e-text); cited by incipit because verse numbers differ between editions. No original given.

paraphrase: What makes a woman a Paṟaicci, what makes her a Brahmin woman (paṉatti)? Is there any difference in their flesh, skin and bone, or in the pleasure they give? Divide them, if you can, and look.
speaker: Sivavākkiyar
